html:
SMTO-SKL-0156 — Your GitHub account changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 3ec16ee4-e859-5d67-88b7-f27dfe874ccb
Slug: github-account-changed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • The saved GitHub account for this request was edited, or its token now signs in as a different GitHub user. SMTO stopped this request before it changed anything on GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to check your GitHub connection. It shows which GitHub login the saved token signs in as. This tells you whether the token and the saved login still belong to the same person.
  2. If they don't match, open Parameter Store, select the GitHub account entry, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, correct the login, account ID or token, and select Save. SMTO refuses to act when the token would act as a different GitHub user than the one saved.
  3. If the account was changed during this conversation, check on github.com whether earlier changes SMTO made in this conversation went to the right place before asking for more. Earlier steps used the account as it was before the change.

What success looks like

  • The connection check shows the GitHub login you expect as verified, and your request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your token into the chat, and don't repeat a change on GitHub until you've checked whether it already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected GitHub Account profile changed revision since it was accepted, the supplied account_id differs from the profile, or the token's live /user login/ID does not match the saved login and account_id.

What this means

  • Accepted profile revisions changed, supplied account_id differs, or live token access finds the saved profile changed. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Accepted profile revisions changed, supplied account_id differs, or live token access finds the saved profile changed.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact account ID and profile revisions, then inspect any earlier receipts.

How to fix it

  • account_changed is raised when an accepted parameter binding's created_at/updated_at no longer match the stored record, when args.account_id differs from the profile, when the record changes between token resolutions, or when GET /user returns a different id/login. Run github.connection_status and github.accounts, correct login/account_id/token so they describe the same principal, and reconcile any earlier writes in the conversation before new work.
  • Inspect github.accounts and github.connection_status again. Reconfirm the exact account ID after a profile or principal change.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Further work uses the deliberately confirmed current account after prior effects are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
